summary: Refine the thirteen accepted GC.6 targets using native root-unit coordinates, the actual torsor comparison, ramified determinant and section checks, two obstruction-sensitive torsor fibre sequences, root-framed support moving from existing function-field weak approximation, and a cyclic tensor trace calculation. The quadratic trace route uses GC.5 signed translation and character determination on the quotient by the actual modified-unit image; it does not use Picard-stack exactness. All targets remain unchecked. Complete denotes a finished planning pass, not implementation or geometric closure.

nodes.title: Root-unit coordinates
nodes.statement: For a homomorphism r:A0 to B0 of commutative rings, rootUnitCoordinates(r) is the native subgroup of A0^units times B0^units cut out by Units.map(r)(u)=v^2. It is the equalizer of the restriction of the first projection and the square of the second projection. It retains both coordinates and their unit proofs. On a framed etale chart this is the section formula for the imported root multiplicative sheaf, not a substitute for its sheaf or stack.
hypotheses: A0 and B0 are commutative rings in arbitrary universes; r is a ring homomorphism. No nontriviality, reducedness, surjectivity of r or invertibility of 2 is needed for this coordinate definition.
proofSteps: Compose the two native product projections with Units.map(r) and the power homomorphism.
Take their existing subgroup equalizer. Restriction maps preserve the defining equality; the geometric comparison is supplied by root-torsor-comparison.
acceptance: The square operation is on units; it is never treated as a ring homomorphism.
The first projection need not be injective, and forgetting the second coordinate is not the definition.

sources.match: The source gives the sheaf formula; the native subgroup is its framed section adapter.

nodes.title: Root frames and the torsor stack
nodes.statement: For every T, the groupoid of C-torsors on (X_T)_et is naturally equivalent to the groupoid of triples (M,J,alpha:J^2 isomorphic to M restricted to R_T). It sends a triple to the sheaf of simultaneous frames (e,f) with alpha(f^2)=e|R_T. Its automorphisms are actual compatible frame changes (u,v) with res(u)=v^2. Likewise B-torsors identify with line bundles on Xprime_T; A-torsors identify with line bundles on X_T. These are symmetric monoidal equivalences natural under arbitrary base change and on all arrows.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.

nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.

On the small etale site of X_T write A=G_m, B=nu_*G_m, C=G_m^sqrtR, N=(Nm,res), K=ker N, j:K to B, q:B to K induced by b/sigma(b), and i:A to B the invariant inclusion. In cohomology use additive notation for these abelian sheaves.
proofSteps: Choose local frames of the two lines. The discrepancy in alpha is a unit on R_T; after an etale refinement lift its square root, using 2 invertible, to obtain simultaneous frames. This proves local nonemptiness of the frame sheaf.

The coordinate subgroup acts simply transitively on simultaneous frames. Conversely extend a C-torsor through the two projections and glue the two trivial lines; the defining equality gives alpha. Cocycle descent makes these inverse on objects and arrows.

For B, apply Stacks Lemma 31.18.1 (0BUT): a line on the inverse image of a finite morphism becomes trivial over the inverse image of a Zariski neighbourhood on the base. Thus its B-frame sheaf is already locally nonempty in the etale topology, for arbitrary T.
Tensor the frame torsors and compare both constructions locally to get monoidal and base-change coherence. Import general descent, never re-plan it.
acceptance: For R empty recover the ordinary Picard groupoid, with its scalar automorphisms.
At a geometric point of R keep both roots of unity as arrow labels.
The result concerns torsors, not arbitrary sections with a square-zero root; no full root-section fibre is replaced by a gerbe.

sources.match: The paper identifies root Picard objects with torsors. The simultaneous-frame equivalence and its arrows are the explicit descent verification.

Tag 03AG supplies torsor local triviality. Lemma 95.14.2 (04UJ) is stated on the big fppf site; its gluing proof is applied here on the small etale site through the generic SF.1/sheaf-stack contract, descending the sheaf, action and local torsor condition. The root-frame and based-fibre comparisons are authored deductions.
Rank-one locally free modules and G_m torsors agree; the finite-cover frame argument supplies the direct-image version.
Line bundles over a finite inverse image trivialize over inverse images of base Zariski neighbourhoods; this proves local nonemptiness of the B-frame torsor without a limit argument.

nodes.title: Ramified determinant and residue square
nodes.statement: On a quadratic chart S0=A0[t]/(t^2-a) with 2 invertible and involution t mapped to -t, the norm of c+d*t is c^2-a*d^2. Modulo a the norm is the square of the image of c. The reduced branch section has t=0; after every base change this gives res Nm(u)=(res_Rprime u)^2 on units and the natural isomorphism (Mprime|Rprime_T)^2 isomorphic to Nm(Mprime)|R_T on lines. For a norm-one unit with residue1 at the branch, w=1+u is locally invertible there and u=w/sigma(w); ordinary norm-one without residue1 does not suffice.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.

nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.

A0 is a local chart ring, a cuts out the branch divisor, and the pulled-back cover is the displayed quadratic algebra. After arbitrary base change a need not be a non-zero-divisor; the determinant identity still holds.
proofSteps: In the basis (1,t), multiplication by c+d*t has matrix with rows (c,a*d) and (d,c); compute its determinant.
Reduce modulo a and use t=0 for the specified Rprime section, retaining the nonreduced inverse-image algebra with t^2=0. Apply the formula to transition units of Mprime, not just to one trivial line.

The residue of w is2. The identity sigma(u)=u inverse gives sigma(w)=w/u, hence local surjectivity of q onto K near R. Away from R split the etale double cover. For ker q, write b=c+d*t: sigma(b)=b forces 2*d=0 and hence d=0, so b is an invariant unit; this remains true after nonflat base change. The invariant inclusion is injective because the chart is free with basis (1,t). Together these calculations give exactness at every term of the parent sheaf complex.

For a target (u,v) in C, choose etale-locally a square root z of u whose restriction along R is v. Such a branch choice extends etale-locally because z squared=u is etale with 2 and u invertible. Then the invariant unit nu^*z has norm u and branch residue v. Away from R the split cover gives surjectivity directly. This proves epimorphism of sheaves, not global sections.
acceptance: For c=0,d=1 the norm is -a, including the sign; its branch restriction is0.
At a=0 the upstairs algebra has t^2=0 and is not replaced by its reduction.
For u=-1, ordinary norm is1 but branch residue is-1; such u is not in ker N when the branch is nonempty.
Etale surjectivity of N is checked by lifting a square root of the first coordinate with the prescribed branch value. It is not asserted on all global sections.

sources.match: The residue-square and sheaf exactness assertions are expanded by this chart calculation.
Finite locally free norm is the multiplication determinant and commutes with base change.

nodes.title: Root norm, torsors and sections agree
nodes.statement: Under root-torsor-comparison, extension of B-torsors through N sends Mprime to (Nm Mprime, Mprime|Rprime_T, alpha), with alpha from the residue-square comparison. This equivalence intertwines tensor product, unit, pullback of T and all their associativity comparisons. On the parent whole section stack it sends (Mprime,sprime) to (Nm Mprime,Mprime|Rprime_T,alpha,Nm sprime,sprime|Rprime_T); the root-section square, the forgetful Abel–Jacobi square and tensor multiplication square commute. This holds also for zero sections. On the fibrewise nonzero open, divisors are pushed forward with residue-field multiplicities.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.

nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.
proofSteps: Apply the norm to transition units in a simultaneous frame. The two resulting cocycles are precisely Nm of the line transition and its branch restriction, so identify the extension torsor with the parent root norm.
The determinant and transition formulas commute with every coefficient change. Check the tensor and unit comparisons in frames, then descend equality of the whole comparisons.
For a section use the determinant of its multiplication map in those frames. The residue-square identity gives the root section. It is polynomial and applies when the section is zero or nilpotent.
On fibrewise nonzero sections use the imported finite-flat divisor norm formula. Degree is preserved by the norm and doubled by pullback, with degrees weighted by residue degrees.
acceptance: Norm(O_Xprime(1))=O_X(1) for the cover P1 to P1, t mapped to t^2; norm is not degree doubling.
A zero section maps to a zero section but its root line is still Mprime|Rprime_T.
A closed point of residue degree f above its image contributes multiplicity f to pushforward; no degree-one-point assumption is made.

sources.match: These are the norm and section diagrams; the comparison with torsor extension and full coherence are explicit refinements.
Norms of line transition maps and sections provide the ordinary construction and base change.

nodes.title: Canonical trivialization of the norm of a difference
nodes.statement: For d(M)=M tensor (sigma^*M)^dual, construct a symmetric monoidal natural trivialization tau_M:N(d(M)) isomorphic to 1_C. Its ordinary norm component is cancellation using Nm(sigma^*M) isomorphic to Nm(M); its branch-root component is the identity between the restrictions of M and sigma^*M along sigma|Rprime=id. The square of the latter component equals the restriction of the former. The resulting functor M mapped to (d(M),tau_M) is the composite of extension through q:B to K and j:K to B with its canonical norm trivialization.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.

nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.

On the small etale site of X_T write A=G_m, B=nu_*G_m, C=G_m^sqrtR, N=(Nm,res), K=ker N, j:K to B, q:B to K induced by b/sigma(b), and i:A to B the invariant inclusion. In cohomology use additive notation for these abelian sheaves.
proofSteps: In a line frame with transition b, the transition of d(M) is b/sigma(b). Its norm is1 and its branch restriction is1, giving a simultaneous unit frame, not merely an isomorphism class.
Descend these compatible frames to tau_M. Norm invariance and evaluation on a line and its dual supply the two components intrinsically.
The local coordinate identity is preserved by every frame change, tensor product and pullback. Descent then supplies naturality and all unit/associativity comparisons.
acceptance: At the branch, trivialize the root line as well as the norm line.
Replacing tau_M by an unrelated norm trivialization is a different datum and must enter the obstruction calculation.
For M=1 the specified trivialization is the unit one, not an arbitrary scalar.

nodes.title: The two torsor fibre sequences
nodes.statement: The exact sheaf complex splits into 0 to A to B to K to0 and 0 to K to B to C to0. On every X_T there are natural symmetric monoidal equivalences Tors(K) equivalent to hofib(Tors(B) to Tors(C)) at the unit C-torsor, and Tors(A) equivalent to hofib(Tors(B) to Tors(K)) at the unit K-torsor. A point of the first fibre is (L,tau:N(L) isomorphic to1); its arrows commute with tau. A point of the second is (M,beta:q_*M isomorphic to1); its arrows commute with beta. The second target is Tors(K), not Tors(B) under d=j q. Both equivalences are effective descent equivalences, natural in T.
hypotheses: k is a finite field of characteristic p different from 2; X/k is a smooth projective geometrically connected curve; R is a reduced finite divisor, possibly empty, and U=X minus R.

nu:Xprime to X is a finite flat double cover, Xprime is smooth projective geometrically connected, sigma is its nonidentity involution, R is exactly its reduced branch divisor, and its reduced ramification divisor Rprime maps isomorphically to R. All family assertions allow arbitrary k-schemes T and use the induced cover of X_T; Rprime_T is this base change, not a new reduction operation.

On the small etale site of X_T write A=G_m, B=nu_*G_m, C=G_m^sqrtR, N=(Nm,res), K=ker N, j:K to B, q:B to K induced by b/sigma(b), and i:A to B the invariant inclusion. In cohomology use additive notation for these abelian sheaves.
proofSteps: For a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves, extend an H-torsor through the inclusion to a G-torsor with its canonical quotient trivialization.

Conversely take the inverse image of the unit section under the given quotient trivialization; local surjectivity makes this an H-torsor. Use actual sheaf pullbacks, so morphisms and inverse comparisons are determined on sections.
Apply this argument to the two short exact sequences. Effective descent glues both torsors and arrows; the constructions commute with restriction and tensor product.
Identify the first fibre geometrically by root-torsor-comparison. Difference-norm-nullhomotopy identifies its distinguished image from Tors(B).
acceptance: Do not replace either homotopy fibre by the ordinary kernel on pi_0.
The automorphisms in the first fibre are H0(K), while those of a descent in the second are H0(A).
Over a split unramified chart q sends (u,v) to(u/v,v/u), and the first kernel is the diagonal copy of A.

gaps.title: Inherited root-stack lisse and Frobenius frontier
gaps.detail: The parent ST-LISSE/ST-OPS gaps and GC.5 signed-character-translation contract still require actual lisse sheaves on the finite tame root stack, their finite-cover/stalk comparison and Frobenius-compatible tensor/dual transport. These are not supplied by native PiTensorProduct or by a scheme-only cohomology theorem. This pass specifies the cyclic stalk calculation and signed/all-degree transport exactly, while retaining the inherited supplier frontier. No full six-functor theory, cohomological point-counting theorem or generic gerbe classification is needed for GC.6.
